papers.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
papers.summary: We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $α$-moment $ν$ for some unknown $α\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures. The reduction is based on empirical residual pruning and is agnostic to the moment exponent, the noise scale, the covariance, and the design moment. Under a finite fourth-moment condition on the covariates, any finite-variance subroutine attaining the sub-Gaussian rate yields the following when the number of samples $n$ is above a suitably defined threshold: Without knowing $α$ or $ν$, we have with probability at least $1-δ$ that $ \|\widehatθ-θ^*\|_Σ \lesssim_α ν^{1/α} \big(\frac{d+\log(1/δ)}{n}\big)^{\frac{α-1}α}, $ where $d$ is the dimension, $Σ$ is the covariate covariance matrix, and $\|v\|_Σ:=(v^\topΣv)^{1/2}$. We further prove a matching minimax lower bound that holds under the same conditions. The reduction is computationally efficient whenever the finite-variance subroutine is. We also obtain a distribution-free prediction guarantee under a bounded raw $α$-moment assumption on the response, and give an analogous $α$-agnostic reduction for mean estimation.
papers.tldr: 無限分散領域における高確率線形回帰を研究し、有限条件付き$α$-モーメントを持つ回帰ノイズに対して、有限分散の回帰手法を弱モーメント手法に変換するブラックボックス還元を提案します。この還元は、サンプル数が適切な閾値を超える場合に、確率$1-δ$で推定誤差が制御されることを示しています。

papers.title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning
papers.summary: This study examines one-day-ahead forecasting of the S&P 500 closing level using a 2006-2025 dataset that includes fundamental price data, macroeconomic indicators, and engineered technical features. We benchmark three model families, namely linear regression, vanilla recurrent neural networks (RNN), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM), within a unified preprocessing and chronological evaluation pipeline. A central contribution of this work is a methodological audit of common practices in the deep-learning-for-stock-prediction literature. We identify three sources of result inflation that frequently appear in published methodologies: wavelet-denoised evaluation targets, the absence of a naive persistence baseline, and best-of-N replicate reporting. We then re-evaluate all model families under a corrected protocol that controls for each. Performance is reported using root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, and the Pearson correlation coefficient, averaged across N = 30 independent replicates per configuration. We compare models on accuracy, stability across replicates, and architectural depth sensitivity, using the naive persistence forecast (predicting today's close as tomorrow's close) as a primary baseline against which all candidate models must demonstrate improvement.
papers.tldr: この研究では、2006年から2025年のデータセットを用いてS&P 500の終値を1日先読みするために、線形回帰、RNN、LSTMの3つのモデルを比較し、深層学習による株価予測における結果の過剰評価の原因を特定しています。結果は、修正されたプロトコルに基づいて再評価され、モデルの精度、安定性、アーキテクチャの深さに対する感度が比較されています。

papers.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
papers.summary: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313$\times$ and prefill latency by 6.9$\times$ at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5$\times$ and overall memory performance by +5.77%. Finally, MemOnce generalizes zero-shot to downstream representation tasks, achieving competitive results against specialized models.
papers.tldr: MemOnceは、大規模言語モデル（LLM）のためのスケーラブルなメモリアーキテクチャで、効率的なメモリ管理を実現し、GPUメモリの使用量を大幅に削減しつつ、計算の複雑さを線形に保つことができる。実験結果では、MemOnceが従来のトランスフォーマーや他のアーキテクチャに対して優れた性能を示し、特にメモリ状態キャッシュを1313倍削減し、スループットを3.5倍向上させた。

papers.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
papers.summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, activity and impulse control. Electroencephalography (EEG) records brain activity as children and adolescents perform cognitive tasks. However, comparing features derived from these recordings requires consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows and documented quality decisions. We curated 669 existing BALLADEER recordings from 156 participants across five task conditions so that researchers can compare seven EEG feature families on the same time intervals for each participant and task. The dataset links continuous signals to precomputed measurements from 115 feature definitions or templates and records the quality decisions made for each recording. Analyses must still account for repeated measurements within participants, residual artefacts and differences between acquisition systems. Technical validation covered signal integrity, numerical checks on feature estimators and completeness of the released files. In every task, the median proportion of recording time retained after preprocessing was 100%. To illustrate reuse, we report saved participant-held-out evaluations comparing XGBoost using all seven families on eight-second windows with a predictor based only on recruitment-group prevalence in the training fold. Recruitment-group discrimination was stronger in Robots than in the three Slackline conditions. These descriptive results from overlapping cohorts do not establish diagnostic validity. The dataset, curation software and aggregate results for the predictive example are publicly available.
papers.tldr: ADHDの分類に関する研究のために、669件のEEG記録を収集し、同一の時間間隔で7つのEEG特徴ファミリーを比較可能にしたデータセットを作成しました。このデータセットは、信号の整合性や特徴推定の数値チェックを行い、公開されているため、研究者が再利用できるようになっています。

papers.title: Non-penetrating World Models
papers.summary: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent. Despite its simplicity, NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%. Remarkably, our method shows zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles. We publicly release our code, the NoPeBench benchmark, and model weights. Project Page: https://nopeworld.github.io .
papers.tldr: 新たな研究では、インタラクティブなビデオワールドモデルにおける物体の侵入を防ぐためのNoPeBenchベンチマークを導入し、既存のオープンソースモデルがこの問題に対処できていないことを明らかにしました。新たに提案されたNoPeWorldフレームワークは、拡散トランスフォーマーの隠れ状態を利用して侵入を予測し、安全な行動に置き換えることで、物理的違反率を74%から16%に大幅に低下させることに成功しました。

papers.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
papers.summary: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's own components during training -- freeing a smaller heterogeneous network inside. We evaluate Model Carving by pre-training standard Transformers from 140M to 2.7B parameters and looped Transformers from 140M to 1.3B. At equal training compute, carved models reach a lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Furthermore, carved models also outperform size-matched models produced by pruning or distillation, suggesting that the best way to obtain small models for edge devices is to carve them during training, not to compress a large one afterwards. This advantage both grows with scale and carries over to downstream tasks such as few-shot evaluation and generation. Because the removed sublayers no longer run, carved models also cost up to 34% fewer FLOPs per token and decode up to 1.6 times faster without cost in quality. Our results show that architecture, like weights, should be learned and not fixed in advance, and that inside every large transformer is a smaller, faster, stronger one waiting to be carved out.
papers.tldr: モデルカービングは、トランスフォーマーの重みとアーキテクチャを同時に学習する手法で、トレーニング中に不要なサブレイヤーを削除することで、より小さく効率的なモデルを生成します。このアプローチにより、従来の密なモデルよりも低い検証損失を達成し、エッジデバイス向けに最適化された小型モデルをトレーニング中に得ることができることが示されました。

papers.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
papers.summary: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) is essential for high predictive performance, but its computational cost becomes prohibitive when candidate configurations require repeated training on large datasets. This paper proposes a ranking-preserving coreset (RPC) selection framework for accelerating evolutionary HPO. The method constructs a compact coreset that preserves the relative ranking of hyperparameter configurations observed on the full training data. Coreset selection is formulated as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes Spearman rank correlation between full-data and subset-based configuration rankings while penalizing subset size. The selected coreset is then used for HPO with three evolutionary algorithms: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Cross-generational elitist Selection, Heterogeneous Recombination and Cataclysmic Mutation (CHC), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Experiments on seven tabular, two text, and two image benchmark datasets show that RPC substantially reduces HPO time while maintaining test accuracy comparable to full-dataset HPO across decision tree, text classification, and image classification tasks. Across datasets and optimizers, HPO-stage speedups range from approximately 1.14x to 8.80x, while the one-time coreset construction cost is accounted for separately through end-to-end runtime and break-even analysis. On 20 held-out configurations excluded from coreset construction, RPC achieves higher ranking correlation than same-size random sampling on 8 of 11 datasets (dataset-level Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p = 0.014). These results show that ranking preservation extends beyond the configurations used during selection. The one-time construction cost can be amortized when the coreset is reused across HPO runs.
papers.tldr: ハイパーパラメータ最適化（HPO）の計算コストを削減するために、相対的なランキングを保持するコアセット選択フレームワーク（RPC）が提案され、実験によりHPO時間を大幅に短縮しつつ、テスト精度を維持できることが示されました。RPCは、選択されたコアセットを用いて、進化的アルゴリズムでのHPOを効率化し、複数のデータセットで優れたランキング相関を達成しました。

papers.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
papers.summary: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$), driving excess distractor mass to zero; (2) a three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule that damps bipartite residuals; (3) an exact rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 Tensor Cores, FP32 potentials); and (4) a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant with verified zero future leakage. On NVIDIA L4, sparsemax THOT trained at $L=128$ reaches 97.40% zero-shot recall of fixed bindings at $L=262{,}144$ under pure task loss ($α=0$) and 98.83% at $α=0.05$ (matched by $O(L)$ thresholded ReLU at $α=0.05$, vs. 80.60% at $α=0$), while softmax-gated hub OT drops to 3.52%. In bidirectional operator microbenchmarks, our kernel runs forward+VJP in 100.1 ms at $H=8, D=64, L=262\mathrm{K}$ (2.2x faster with 4.0x smaller compiler temporaries than latent softmax) and 1.34 ms vs. 4.37 ms for cuDNN FlashAttention at $L=4{,}096$; multi-layer LM runs use the unfused path. Zero-shot WikiText-103 multi-needle retrieval hits 100.00% (128/128 queries at $L=65\mathrm{K}$) vs. 0.78% for short-trained RoPE FlashAttention, and compact 4-layer WikiText-4K runs show modest causal and masked LM gains.
papers.tldr: Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT)は、長文コンテキストモデルにおける情報の希薄化を解消し、効率的な注意機構を実現する新しい手法で、NVIDIA L4上で高いリコール率を達成しています。特に、THOTは、従来の手法に比べて処理速度が向上し、ゼロショットの情報検索タスクで優れた性能を示しています。

papers.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Agnostic PAC Learning for Partial Concept Classes
papers.summary: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\{-1,+1,\star\}^{\mathcal X}$ be a partial concept class of finite VC dimension $d$. We construct a deterministic agnostic PAC learner that, for every $\varepsilon,δ\in(0,1)$, uses $O((d+\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon^2)$ i.i.d. examples from an arbitrary distribution $\mathcal D$ over $\mathcal X\times\{-1,+1\}$ and returns a total concept $\hat h:\mathcal X\to\{-1,+1\}$ satisfying $\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(\hat h)\leq \min_{h\in\mathcal H}\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(h)+\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-δ$, where $\text{er}_{\mathcal D}(h)=\mathbb P_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal D}[h(x)\neq y]$. This establishes the optimal sample complexity, matching the lower bound of Alon et al. (FOCS 2021).
papers.tldr: 部分概念クラスに対するアグノスティックPAC学習の最適サンプル複雑性を示し、任意の分布からの独立同分布サンプルを用いて、エラー率が指定された許容範囲内に収束する学習器を構築した。

papers.title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
papers.summary: Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. We find that most top-ranked errors of a strong corpus-level scorer come from choosing the wrong video, not from imprecise boundaries, and that re-weighting the evidence the scorer already uses does not fix them. We present DiTraR, which addresses video selection from two complementary directions. A witness-interval scorer decomposes the query into probes and scores every candidate interval of every corpus video exactly; a multi-scorer energy ensemble averages the energies of independently trained scorers before one exhaustive search; and a transcript verifier, a frozen language model that reads the time-stamped dialogue of the highest-ranked videos, re-orders the moments without changing their boundaries. With all settings frozen on development data and a single evaluation, DiTraR reaches 24.36 and 13.55 R@1 at IoU 0.5 and 0.7 on the TVR validation split. The ensemble improves queries about visual content, the verifier improves queries about dialogue, and their gains largely add up.
papers.tldr: DiTraRは、動画コーパスからの瞬間検索において、誤った動画選択を改善するために、プローブを用いたウィットネス間スコアラーとマルチスコアエネルギーアンサンブルを組み合わせ、さらにトランスクリプト検証を行う手法を提案し、TVRバリデーションスプリットで高い精度を達成しました。

papers.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
papers.summary: Despite major advances in structure prediction, modelling the motions and interactions that drive biomolecular function at scale remains a central challenge. We introduce BioEmu2, a generative model for atomically resolved biomolecular structures combining static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution, that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD). Trained on experimental and synthetic structures and extensive MD data, it supports multi-component systems containing proteins, nucleic acids, modified residues, ligands and ions. Structure-prediction accuracy is comparable to top open-weight biomolecular folding models, and a context parallel mode enables prediction of megadalton complexes. Equilibrium distributions approximate MD references with free-energy errors near 1 kcal/mol across tested proteins and complexes. Time propagation predicts long-timescale dynamical trajectories and kinetics of binding and conformational changes. Generated structures can be controlled by conditioning on residue contacts or steering with user-defined bias potentials. Enhanced sampling enables free energy calculation involving rare states. BioEmu2 makes the study of biomolecular ensembles and dynamics scalable.
papers.tldr: BioEmu2は、静的構造予測、平衡サンプリング、時間発展を組み合わせた生成モデルで、分子動力学よりも桁違いに速くバイオ分子の動態をエミュレートし、複雑なシステムの構造予測とダイナミクスの研究をスケーラブルにします。

papers.title: ESSI: Computationally Efficient Semantic Search for Sparse Autoencoder Concepts
papers.summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose diffusion model activations into interpretable features, but steering a model with them requires identifying which features map to a given semantic concept, if any. Existing methods for this concept to feature task are expensive, relying on grid searches or repeated passes through the frozen UNet. We propose Efficient Semantic Sparse Identification (ESSI). Using segmentation masks to label SDXL activations as concept or non-concept, ESSI ranks SAE features and binary-searches for the smallest set on which a linear classifier still separates positive from negative samples while not falling below a performance threshold, then reuses that classifier to calibrate the steering strength. We evaluate the same selected features on both concept insertion and object unlearning. Compared with prior work, ESSI is as cheap or cheaper, and performs well on both insertion and removal.
papers.tldr: ESSI（Efficient Semantic Sparse Identification）は、スパースオートエンコーダーを用いて、概念に基づく特徴を効率的に特定する手法であり、従来の高コストな方法に比べて安価でありながら、概念の挿入とオブジェクトの忘却の両方で優れた性能を発揮します。

papers.title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
papers.summary: Reward-independent representations enable reinforcement learning agents to reuse knowledge across tasks, but limited representation capacity raises three fundamental questions: what statistical dependence should these representations capture, which components of that dependence should be retained for policy improvement, and how does discarding the remaining components affect decision-making? We address these questions through canonical dependence analysis. For a reference policy, we construct an action-centered, positive-lag canonical dependence matrix (CDM) that isolates the additional predictive contribution of the current action beyond the current state. Its singular value decomposition yields Spectral Universal Advantage Features (SUAF), paired features that recover delayed advantage through linear reward projections. We show that the spectrum quantifies mutual information between current action and future state-action visitation conditioned on current state and determines reward specific approximation errors. Retaining the leading modes gives optimal rank-constrained approximations under both isotropic average-case and reward-uniform minimax criteria. Separating the immediate reward contrast also avoids the spectral floor arising from direct compression of the full advantage operator. To learn SUAF from reward-free data, we develop an action-centered Soft-HGR objective with bidirectional temporal-difference estimation. We further connect spectral approximation errors to sufficient conditions for policy improvement. Finite-state experiments validate the spectral predictions and feature-learning method, while zero-shot evaluations on discrete tasks and continuous-control benchmarks demonstrate the utility of the learned representations across rewards.
papers.tldr: SUAF（Spectral Universal Advantage Features）は、強化学習エージェントが報酬に依存せずに知識を再利用できるようにするための新しい特徴表現を提案し、行動中心の正の遅延共分散行列を用いて、政策改善に必要な情報を抽出する手法を示しています。このアプローチは、報酬のないデータから学習し、ゼロショット評価においても有効性を確認しています。

papers.title: Augmentation of cardiovascular flow measurements with generative diffusion models
papers.summary: Cardiovascular imaging offers several ways to measure blood flow, but each provides an incomplete, resolution-limited, or noisy view of the underlying dynamics. Reconstructing the missing information is inherently ambiguous because several flow fields may be compatible with the same observation. Here, we investigate generative diffusion models as tools for cardiovascular-flow generation and reconstruction using a fully controlled state-of-the-art dataset from a digital twin of a healthy human left heart. First, we show how unconditional samples reproduce the changing anatomy and the highly fluctuating statistical properties of the flow throughout the cardiac cycle. Second, we test the conditional inference of our generative model by reconstructing an entire 2D planar section of geometry and flow configurations from a limited portion. Repeated reconstructions allow us to represent a range of plausible completions, going beyond a single deterministic estimate, while their mean retains the principal features of the reference flow. Comparison with a Gaussian process regression baseline on the same reduced domain highlights the main advantage of diffusion models: their reconstructed ensembles capture a broader range of velocity and gradient fluctuations, better encompassing ground-truth features that the baseline distributions can miss. Our results provide a quantitative proof of concept for probabilistic reconstruction of incomplete cardiovascular-flow measurements and demonstrate the potential for groundbreaking applications to the augmentation of in-vivo cardiovascular imaging data.
papers.tldr: 心血管フロー測定のために、生成拡散モデルを用いて不完全なデータからの再構築を行い、従来の手法よりも幅広い速度や勾配の変動を捉えることができることを示しました。このアプローチは、in-vivo心血管イメージングデータの拡張に向けた革新的な応用の可能性を示唆しています。

papers.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints. This makes metric 3D inference inherently ambiguous and leaves it unclear whether their spatial predictions are grounded in visual evidence or driven primarily by semantic priors. In contrast, calibrated stereo provides explicit cross-view geometry that resolves this ambiguity and offers a more reliable foundation for metric 3D perception and geometric generalization. We investigate how VLMs can learn transferable 3D representations directly from calibrated binocular observations. To this end, we introduce StereoVLM, the first geometry-aware binocular VLM for metric 3D spatial reasoning. StereoVLM follows a hierarchical learning paradigm spanning from cross-view correspondence and disparity estimation to calibration-conditioned metric depth perception and semantic spatial reasoning. We further find that disparity supervision generalizes substantially better than direct binocular depth supervision on unseen environments. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Stereo3D-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark across three levels, from point-level geometry to object-level spatial reasoning. StereoVLM-8B achieves 95.17% depth accuracy ($δ_1$) and a 66.98 average object-level score on Stereo3D-Bench. Intervention results further indicate that the model's performance on Stereo3D-Bench benefits from valid cross-view geometry and cannot be explained solely by additional visual tokens or semantic priors. Hierarchical geometric supervision also yields average gains of 3.54 points across five spatial benchmarks and 4.3 percentage points in RoboCasa manipulation success.
papers.tldr: StereoVLMは、キャリブレーションされた双眼観察から直接学習することで、物理的な3D空間のメトリック推論を行う初のジオメトリ対応の双眼視覚言語モデルです。このモデルは、クロスビューの幾何学的情報を活用し、深度精度95.17%を達成し、従来の手法よりも優れた一般化能力を示しています。

papers.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
papers.summary: Detecting individual instances is crucial for many segmentation problems. However, expert instance annotations are often unavailable, so instances are approximated heuristically (e.g., as connected components of semantic maps), which can merge touching objects or split fragmented ones. Even when expert annotations exist, expert disagreement or structural delineation biases can yield split or merged reference instances, corresponding to over- or under-segmentation, respectively. Panoptic Quality (PQ) and related metrics capture both segmentation and detection quality while weighting all instances equally, regardless of size. Yet when the references are biased, these metrics can neither detect split or merged instances nor distinguish valid from invalid overor under-segmentation. We present Star Panoptic Quality (StarPQ), a novel evaluation ramework, which closes this gap in two steps: First, we construct a so-called star forest in the bipartite graph whose clean, merge, and split stars isolate different failure modes. Second, we calculate the final metric by individually weighting each failure mode, allowing practitioners to account for instance delineation biases. Across various experiments, we demonstrate that StarPQ not only enables targeted penalization or eniency towards specific failure modes, but also serves as a diagnostic tool to reveal their prevalence.
papers.tldr: Star Panoptic Quality (StarPQ)は、分割や統合されたインスタンスの評価において、バイアスのある参照データを考慮し、異なる失敗モードを個別に重み付けすることで、セグメンテーションと検出の質を向上させる新しい評価フレームワークです。これにより、特定の失敗モードに対するペナルティや寛容さを調整できるだけでなく、その発生頻度を診断するツールとしても機能します。

papers.title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
papers.summary: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. We study how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, introducing an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component, i.e., the computation that appears only when a specified set of layers acts together under identity ablation. Tracking this quantity across public checkpoints of Pythia, OLMo, and Amber yields three findings. First, write-relative connected coordination strengthens from its initialization or earliest-checkpoint baseline as pretraining proceeds, across all measured interaction orders. Second, these connected components are behaviorally consequential under direct intervention: deleting them damages perplexity more than deleting a norm-matched random direction at the same site in all 35 measured model-order cells. Third, pairwise representation similarity is consistently negatively correlated with pairwise connected coordination across seven models, yet the two signals are not interchangeable: similarity- and coordination-based block-removal criteria often agree in Pythia but diverge on Amber. Together, these results suggest that architectural depth provides the opportunity for sequential computation, while pretraining progressively organizes cross-layer dependencies within that depth.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: トランスフォーマーは深さに応じて性能が向上するが、層の相互依存性が重要であり、プレトレーニングを通じて層間の依存関係が組織化されることが示された。具体的には、層が一緒に機能する際の計算が重要であり、その削除はモデルの性能に大きな影響を与える。

papers.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
papers.summary: Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. As agents act on these records, both tasks require auditable reasons. Dense embeddings perform well but offer opaque coordinates, cannot be filtered by meaning, and require corpus re-encoding to add new properties. We propose interpretable embeddings built from decision columns: each column stores a decision model's calibrated answer to a natural-language question, with outcomes yes, no, or not stated. A record's embedding is its answers across an ordered set of questions. Similarity decomposes exactly into per-question contributions, and new questions add coordinates without altering existing ones. On public product benchmarks, question-space retrieval matches dense candidate generation statistically in a retrieve-then-verify entity matcher, while providing exact explanations for accepted matches. Questions derived from retrieval failures triple mean reciprocal rank without re-encoding prior answers. For search, inferring the attributes of a suitable result outperforms encoding only the literal request, and combining question-space and dense scores improves retrieval, though not at our prespecified confidence threshold. A single small neural network predicts the full interpretable vector from an existing dense embedding, enabling corpus backfilling from a few thousand labeled rows at roughly 1/200 the cost. We position interpretable embeddings as a complementary, readable retrieval channel for explaining matches, filtering on attributes, and extending indexes as failures expose missing facts.
papers.tldr: ビジネスデータシステムにおけるエンティティマッチングと検索のために、決定列から構築された解釈可能な埋め込みを提案し、これにより記録の類似性を質問ごとに分解し、新しい質問を追加しても既存の情報を変更せずに検索精度を向上させることができる。

papers.title: AnimalFarm: Auditing the Generation and Detection of Hateful Images Featuring Anthropomorphic Characters
papers.summary: Anthropomorphic non-human characters have long been used to convey hateful messages targeting human groups, from Nazi-era propaganda to recent AI-generated imagery on social media. However, the safety risks posed by such imagery remain largely unexplored. We thus conduct the first systematic study of hateful image generation and detection involving anthropomorphic non-human characters. We construct a benchmark from conservatively screened source scenes, covering five character types and three image generation tasks: text-to-image generation, image editing, and conversational image generation. Across 14,250 scheduled queries, image generation systems produce images for 92.1\% of queries, of which 95.9\% contain hateful content. We further collect 4,370 hateful images and evaluate five popular hateful-content detectors. Even the strongest detector, GPT-5.5, identifies only 73.9\% of hateful images, while most detect fewer than 58\%. Our analysis reveals that existing detectors often misclassify hateful images as benign when their main subjects are non-human characters. We explore two effective mitigation approaches: a training-free pipeline that maps non-human characters back to human representations before classification and a detector fine-tuned for this type of hateful content. These approaches achieve F1 scores of 0.962 and 0.979, respectively. Our findings expose significant safety gaps in both image generation and hateful-content detection. Disclaimer: This paper contains hateful text and imagery.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: 本研究では、擬人化キャラクターを用いた憎悪的画像の生成と検出のシステム的な調査を行い、生成された画像の92.1%が憎悪的内容を含むことを発見しました。既存の検出器は、擬人化キャラクターを対象とした憎悪的画像を正確に識別できず、提案された新しいアプローチは高い精度を示しました。

papers.title: QuantStream3D: Geometry-Aligned Low-Bit KV Cache Quantization for Streaming Visual Geometry Transformers
papers.summary: Streaming visual geometry transformers retain historical key-value (KV) states as cross-view geometric memory, but growing caches constrain long-sequence inference. We systematically characterize KV quantization in streaming geometry and uncover two linked challenges: Nonuniform Geometric Sensitivity and Cache-Geometry Mismatch. Quantization sensitivity varies across precision choices and cache locations, while perturbed retrieval changes geometry-head inputs and propagates through subsequent predictions and KV writes. Guided by these findings, we propose QuantStream3D, to our knowledge the first dedicated KV quantization framework for streaming visual geometry transformers. Geometry-Guided Mixed-Precision KV Quantization protects sensitive cross-view evidence, while Geometry-Aligned Quantization-Aware Distillation jointly adapts transformer blocks and geometry heads on student-generated quantized history. Across five benchmarks and two backbones, QuantStream3D achieves near-lossless geometric accuracy in most settings with predominantly 2-bit KV caches, and many configurations surpass unquantized inference. Compared with LLM-oriented KV quantizers, it reduces TUM absolute trajectory error and NeuralRGBD completeness error by up to 57.4% and 69.7%, respectively. Integration with existing native cache-pruning methods further pushes compression while improving reconstruction quality on NeuralRGBD. Our optimized StreamVGGT backend achieves $5.05\times$ physical KV compression and 23.1% lower latency at batch size one. Under a fixed memory budget on the same GPU, it supports $5.4\times$ the maximum batch size and up to $1.67\times$ the peak throughput of unquantized inference. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be made publicly available.
papers.tldr: QuantStream3Dは、ストリーミング視覚幾何トランスフォーマー向けに設計された初のKV量子化フレームワークで、2ビットKVキャッシュを用いてほぼ損失のない幾何精度を達成し、従来の未量子化推論を上回る性能を示します。これにより、物理KV圧縮を5.05倍、レイテンシを23.1%削減し、最大バッチサイズを5.4倍に拡大することが可能です。

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
papers.summary: Electronic health records (EHRs) contain rich health information for uncovering latent patient representations and clinically meaningful subgroups. Learning from EHR data across institutions is valuable because representations learned at a single site may reflect local data patterns and lack generalizability, yet pooling patient-level records across institutions is often impractical because of privacy constraints and communication costs. We propose a communication-efficient, non-iterative federated spectral method for learning shared latent representation components from multi-institutional EHRs, in which each institution shares aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary while keeping patient-level records local. A central server aggregates these summaries with the pooled marginal frequencies to recover both the shared low-rank structure and the canonical row-normalization direction required for interpretable representation recovery. We prove row-wise recovery guarantees and error bounds, with a leading federated variance term matching a corresponding lower bound under explicit regularity conditions. Simulations show that our method closely matches pooled analysis in estimating latent representation components, improves as more sites contribute summaries, and outperforms single-site and existing federated benchmarks across a range of data settings. Applied to real-world multi-facility EHR data for stroke patients, the method learns interpretable patient representations that highlight clinically distinct subgroups and could help inform subgroup-specific care.
papers.tldr: 多施設の電子健康記録（EHR）からの潜在患者表現を学習するために、プライバシー制約と通信コストを考慮した通信効率の良い非反復的フェデレーテッドスペクトル手法を提案し、実際のデータに基づいて臨床的に意味のあるサブグループを特定することができる。シミュレーション結果は、提案手法が既存の単一サイトおよびフェデレーテッドベンチマークを上回る性能を示している。

papers.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
papers.summary: Sustaining user experience (UX) quality in large-scale web search requires scalable evaluation. Traditional surveys are slow and bottleneck rapid A/B testing, while automated metrics often lack the granularity to diagnose visual-spatial UX anomalies. To address this, we introduce the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, a novel industrial architecture for automated UX attribution. Tier 1 (Macro System) acts as a scalable user sentiment regression detector, utilizing a fine-tuned encoder-decoder LLM (based on Gemini XS) on telemetry features. Through multi-task regularization and contextual feature engineering, this tier achieves a +9.8% PR-AUC gain on over 500,000 held-out records, matching baseline recall on all validated regressions with $\sim$20% relative precision gain among the 12 held-out experiments. In production, it reduces measurement latency from weeks to hours and cuts survey overhead by over 40%. Tier 2 (Micro System) provides granular diagnostics by employing a Multimodal LLM (Gemini 3.0 Pro) to natively assess visual renderings and spatial layout of web result blocks, quantifying "User Toil" as the estimated effort required to reach a satisfactory result. Enhanced by RL-based automated prompt optimization and an AI judge for win/loss patterns, the MLLM yields a $>$6.5% F1 score improvement, offering deep insights into content quality and layout friction. Ultimately, this framework enables scalable, accurate, and diagnostic UX attribution, processing O(100k) live experiment queries daily.
papers.tldr: Dual-Tier Sentiment Frameworkは、大規模なウェブ検索におけるユーザーエクスペリエンス（UX）の評価を自動化し、スケーラブルかつ迅速に行うための新しいアーキテクチャで、Tier 1はユーザーの感情を回帰分析し、Tier 2は視覚的な要素とレイアウトの診断を行い、UXの質を向上させる。

papers.title: TEA-Bench-BR: Can Coding Agents Turn a Branching Clinical Specification into Correct Code?
papers.summary: Coding agents increasingly implement rules written by domain experts, and bugs in such code are silent: it runs and returns a plausible answer. We introduce TEA-Bench-BR, a benchmark built on the Brazilian pathway for early autism (TEA) screening: three fictitious instruments with the structure of real ones, a multi-professional referral flow, and export to FHIR R4 with the national RNDS profiles, all specified in Portuguese. A generator samples each task's parameters (144 tasks, 6,798 hidden cases), and the hidden cases kill all 1,955 non-equivalent mutants of the reference. With Gemma 4 as the agent, the 12B solves 38.0% of single-instrument tasks and none at the FHIR level; the 31B solves 77.8%, 85.2% and 78.7% at levels 1 to 3 and passes over 99% of the hidden cases, its remaining failures mostly in input validation rather than clinical decisions. With the same tasks in English, the 31B solves 57.4% at level 3, as its code validates an identifier less often; the 12B's, more often. The 12B misses 10.10% of the cases that call for referral; the 31B, 0.02%. A contamination probe on a modified PHQ-9 finds no error that follows the original rules.
papers.tldr: TEA-Bench-BRは、ブラジルの早期自閉症スクリーニングのためのベンチマークで、コーディングエージェントが臨床仕様を正確なコードに変換できるかを検証するもので、Gemma 4と31Bエージェントが異なるタスクを解決する能力を比較した結果、31Bが高い成功率を示した。

papers.title: FairITR: Fairness-Aware Learning of Multicategory Individualized Treatment Rules
papers.summary: Individualized treatment rules (ITRs) recommend treatment decisions based on individual characteristics and can improve treatment outcomes beyond traditional one-size-fits-all strategies. However, similar to other commonly used algorithmic decision-making methods, ITRs without considering model fairness may result in unfair decisions across groups defined by sensitive attributes, such as race or gender. Although extensive methods have been developed for ITR estimation, most focus solely on optimizing treatment outcomes, while research on fairness-aware ITRs remains limited. Moreover, the practical scenario of multicategory treatments is rarely considered in existing fair ITR studies. To address these gaps, we introduce a fairness notion for multicategory ITRs that requires treatment decisions to be independent of sensitive attributes, and then formulate the corresponding problem of estimating fair ITRs. To solve this problem, we further propose FairITR, a fairness-aware learning framework that jointly optimizes treatment outcomes and fairness. FairITR builds on angle-based classification for multicategory ITR learning and integrates adversarial learning with covariance-based regularization to mitigate unfairness in treatment decisions. A theoretical justification for the fairness properties induced by the adversarial debiasing mechanism is also provided. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that FairITR substantially reduces unfairness in ITRs while maintaining competitive treatment values relative to existing baselines.
papers.tldr: FairITRは、多カテゴリーの個別化治療ルール（ITR）において、感受性属性に依存しない治療決定を求める公平性の概念を導入し、治療成果と公平性を共同最適化するフレームワークを提案します。実験結果は、FairITRが既存の基準と比較して不公平性を大幅に低減しつつ、競争力のある治療効果を維持することを示しています。

papers.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
papers.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by preparing candidate continuations before the target model generates them. Its efficiency depends on how well limited drafting computation anticipates the path the target will actually follow. Anticipating this path involves two sources of uncertainty: the target model's predictions and the randomness of sampling. Yet the former requires a target-model forward pass, while the latter can be fixed before drafting. Building on this observation, we introduce DICE (Draw-Informed Candidate Selection), which pre-samples and synchronizes verification randomness across drafting and verification. By combining these known draws with predictions from an existing drafter, DICE allocates computation toward continuations more likely to be used in the current sampling run. This principle guides node selection throughout draft-tree construction and extends to asynchronous prefetching, where DICE predicts which next-round drafts to prepare. Without additional drafter training or changes to the target sampling distribution, DICE achieves state-of-the-art decoding throughput across diverse settings, with speedups of up to 24.6pp over strong baselines.
papers.tldr: DICE（Draw-Informed Candidate Selection）は、言語モデルの推論を加速するために、事前に候補の続きのサンプリングと検証のランダム性を同期させる手法であり、追加のトレーニングなしで最高のデコーディングスループットを達成し、強力なベースラインに対して最大24.6ppの速度向上を実現します。

papers.title: Renormalized Entropy from Symmetries: Simplicity Bias and Neural Heat Death
papers.summary: Neural networks have parameter symmetries: parameter transformations that do not affect the represented function. How do these symmetries affect the functions that neural networks ultimately learn? We study the implicit bias arising from these symmetries by calculating the equilibrium distribution over represented functions under Langevin dynamics with Gaussian regularization. To isolate the effect of symmetries on this distribution, we study the limit in which the strength of the regularization is taken to zero. In certain cases, we show that the zero-regularization and infinite-time limits commute. In the low temperature limit, we recover known effective regularizations. At positive temperature, a renormalization procedure allows us to derive a novel entropy which predicts symmetry-induced preference for certain functions. For linear networks, we obtain explicit entropy terms that favor singular and low-rank functions. For networks with homogeneous activations, we find entropy terms that favor inactive neurons, which can lead to neural "heat death" in which equilibrium mass concentrates on networks with vanishing output. We interpret these results through the neural tangent kernel, as a simplicity bias selecting for functions that vary slowly under variations in the parameters.
papers.tldr: 神経ネットワークのパラメータ対称性が学習する関数に与える影響を研究し、ガウス正則化下での平衡分布を計算することで、対称性が特定の関数を好む傾向を示す新たなエントロピーを導出しました。この結果、特に線形ネットワークでは特異な低ランク関数を好む傾向があり、同時に均一な活性化を持つネットワークでは非活性ニューロンが好まれ、最終的に「熱的死」に至る可能性があることが示

papers.title: Interpretable Tissue Architecture Complements Pathology Foundation Models
papers.summary: Tissue architecture provides important information for histopathological assessment, yet its complementary predictive value alongside pathology foundation-model representations remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates whether interpretable measurements of cellular and multicellular tissue organization provide additional predictive information beyond learned representations. We introduce a 139-dimensional cellular-to-community representation comprising nine feature groups characterizing nuclear morphology, cellular composition, spatial connectivity, community organization, and cell-cell interactions. Their predictive contributions are systematically evaluated independently and through feature-level fusion with CTransPath and PLIP embeddings using multiple-instance learning (MIL). On the BCNB dataset, estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR) classification is evaluated across four MIL architectures using five-fold patient-disjoint cross-validation. Selected CTransPath fusion configurations achieved mean ROC-AUC values of 0.9144 (ER) and 0.8360 (PR), while PLIP fusion achieved 0.8791 and 0.8015, respectively. Patient-level analyses identified ER-associated differences in nuclear morphology, graph connectivity, cellular communities, and cell-cell interactions. On LungHist700, selected fusion configurations achieved higher mean ROC-AUC across four classification tasks, including adenocarcinoma versus squamous cell carcinoma (0.7967 versus 0.7137 for CTransPath alone). Overall, these findings suggest that interpretable tissue-architecture descriptors can complement foundation-model representations while providing measurable insights into histopathological organization.
papers.tldr: 組織アーキテクチャの解釈可能な測定が、病理学の基盤モデルと組み合わせることで、細胞および多細胞組織の予測情報を追加的に提供することを示す研究が行われ、特にエストロゲン受容体（ER）やプロゲステロン受容体（PR）の分類において高いROC-AUC値を達成しました。これにより、組織アーキテクチャの記述が病理学的評価において重要な役割を果たすことが示唆されました。

papers.title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
papers.summary: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it relies on, and leaves every number to a deterministic guideline engine. On four public longitudinal CT datasets, LesionAgent tracks more lesions and measures them more accurately than every automatic baseline, and where the same 3D models chained by fixed rules call progression falsely at 33 of 56 follow-ups, it does so twice. On clinical follow-up CTs, it agrees with the radiologists' response at 20 of 23 follow-ups, including every change in response, and without training on DeepLesion, it retrieves more of its lesions than every tracker trained on it (89.0% vs. 87.4%). Its harness, not its LLM, makes the difference: given the same LLM and 3D models but not the harness, Claude Code reaches a detection F1 of 41% and LesionAgent 78%, and an open-weight LLM that can run inside the hospital rises from 6% to 73%. LesionAgent and a napari reading app for any LLM are available at https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/LesionAgent.
papers.tldr: LesionAgentは、特定のトレーニングなしで腫瘍の追跡と反応評価を行うエージェントであり、従来の自動化手法よりも多くの病変をより正確に測定し、放射線科医の判断と高い一致率を示しています。詳細はGitHubで公開されています。

papers.title: From Gist to Verbatim: The Controllable Path of One Image Through a Diffusion Prior
papers.summary: Modern generative models are typically studied for their ability to generalize, while memorization is treated as a failure mode. We invert this perspective and ask how a generative model can recall a single datum. We frame memorization as a control problem: a learned conditioning signal steers a frozen diffusion model toward a target image, and we follow the formation of this memory throughout training. Before converging to exact reproduction (verbatim), memory passes through a regime of abstraction: samples preserve the target's semantic content (gist) while remaining diverse in appearance, leaving predictable detail to the generative prior. This semantic organization emerges despite the absence of labels, captions, or any explicit semantic objective. In the abstraction regime, the learned memory approaches ordinary text conditioning and supports editing, one-shot recognition, and retrieval more effectively than in the near-perfect reconstruction regime. These results suggest that memorization can serve as a probe of the relevance structure encoded by a generative model: what must be stored about a datum, what can be reconstructed from prior knowledge, and how learned memories interpolate between reconstructive recall and literal data storage.
papers.tldr: 生成モデルの記憶を制御問題として捉え、特定の画像を再現する過程を探求した研究では、記憶が抽象的な段階を経て最終的に正確な再現に至ることが示され、これにより生成モデルがデータの重要な構造をどのようにエンコードしているかが明らかになった。

papers.title: Beyond Visual Fidelity: Comparing Categorical and Continuous World Models
papers.summary: Visual world models can now generate compelling interactive worlds, but visual realism does not guarantee faithful dynamics. We systematically compare how categorical and continuous prediction shape learned dynamics under both next-token and iterative whole-frame generation. These choices are often bundled in approaches such as autoregressive token models and whole-frame flow matching. We design controlled 2D and 3D environments and evaluate dynamics validity, calibration, and visual quality. In 2D with lossless visual encoding, categorical models achieve higher rollout validity with less training compute, particularly for stochastic entities. Among categorical models, greedy decoding produces the highest rollout validity, while sampling from a next-token model yields the best-calibrated stochastic predictions. Failures in continuous models, such as disappearing game characters, echo those seen in more complex environments. Here, known dynamics let us measure their impact. In 3D, categorical models also achieve stronger long-horizon performance with less training compute. Even models with lossy tokenization remain competitive on semantic accuracy and FVD, despite lower next-frame RGB accuracy. Together, these findings make a strong case for categorical prediction as a compute-efficient route to learning world dynamics.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: カテゴリカルモデルは、連続モデルに比べてトレーニング計算量が少なく、特に確率的エンティティに対して高いロールアウトの妥当性を達成し、3D環境でも優れた長期パフォーマンスを示すことが確認され、世界のダイナミクスを学習するための計算効率の良い手法としての有用性が示された。

papers.title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence with Learning Style Models: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.summary: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has emerged as a powerful tool for transforming learning. This review examines how Generative AI can be integrated with established learning style models (VARK, Kolb, Felder-Silverman, and Honey & Mumford) to support student engagement in large online classes. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar (2015 to 2026) and included 41 studies that met the eligibility criteria. The review maps Generative AI capabilities to learning style preferences, synthesizes existing implementations, highlights benefits and challenges, and proposes pathways for future research and practice. Despite ongoing debates regarding the empirical validity of learning styles, Generative AI enables flexible, multimodal, and real-time adaptation. This study offers practical insights for educators and developers seeking to build more effective, learner centered learning systems
papers.tldr: TL;DR: 本レビューは、生成的人工知能（Generative AI）と学習スタイルモデル（VARK、Kolb、Felder-Silverman、Honey & Mumford）の統合を検討し、大規模オンラインクラスでの学生のエンゲージメントを支援する方法を探ります。生成的AIは学習スタイルに基づく柔軟で多様な適応を可能にし、教育者や開発者にとって実践的な洞察を提供します。

papers.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Specification-guided reinforcement learning (RL) translates formal specifications of desired behavior of agents into shaped rewards. This paper introduces SLICR, a significant paradigm shift that advances the state of the art to specification-guided RL in adversarial settings under partial observability. We employ Strategy Logic (SL), which allows explicit quantification over agents' strategies and uses the linear temporal logic (LTL) to specify the agents' objectives and constraints. This enables reasoning not only about how agents should act to satisfy a specification, but also about how they should respond to the strategies and behaviors of other agents. We evaluate SLICR on three popular benchmarks: Predator-Prey, Google Research Football, and our home-grown extension of SMAC-HARD, demonstrating its effectiveness, scalability, and ability to adapt to diverse adversarial strategies.
papers.tldr: SLICRは、部分観測下の敵対的環境における仕様ガイド強化学習の新しいパラダイムであり、戦略論理（SL）と線形時間論理（LTL）を用いてエージェントの行動を明示的に定量化し、他のエージェントの戦略に応じた反応を可能にします。実験では、Predator-Prey、Google Research Football、SMAC-HARDの拡張版などのベンチマークでその効果とスケーラビリティを示しました。

papers.title: OpenAHBU: Open-sourced Automatic Human Behaviour Understanding Toolkit Through Facial Behaviour Analysis
papers.summary: Automatic facial behaviour understanding (AFBU) is fundamental to various human-centred applications, yet existing academically available toolkits offer limited functionality, closed training pipelines, and weak generalisation. This paper presents OpenAHBU, a fully open-sourced, generalisable toolkit integrating 11 AFBU functions across three semantic levels: (i) short-term external facial attributes, including landmarks, blendshapes, Action Units, and expressions; (ii) short-term facial behaviour-related human psychological states, including valence/arousal and pain; and (iii) long-term facial behaviour-related psychological traits, including depression and personality. Particularly, we re-developed eight functions, where at least four deep learning models covering different computational complexities are developed for each function, providing flexible deployment on resource-constrained and high-throughput computing scenarios. More importantly, models of most functions are trained on a comprehensive corpus aggregating multiple academically available datasets, ensuring robust cross-dataset generalisability.In addition, we include a Synergistic Multi-task Enhancement (SMTE) module to efficiently and adaptively enhance each OpenAHBU function by leveraging the complementary cues contained in its most-related support function's predictions.Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our OpenAHBU outperformed existing open-source toolkits not only in functional coverage but also the predictive performances, while providing superior deployment flexibility across diverse computational scenarios.With fully publicly available training and inference scripts, pre-trained weights, user-friendly GUI, Python library, and cross-platform compatibility, our OpenAHBU provides a reproducible, scalable and extensible toolkit at https://github.com/OpenAHBU/OpenAHBU.
papers.tldr: OpenAHBUは、顔の行動分析を通じて自動的に人間の行動を理解するためのオープンソースツールキットで、11のAFBU機能を統合し、異なる計算複雑性を持つ深層学習モデルを提供します。このツールキットは、既存のオープンソースツールキットよりも機能のカバレッジと予測性能で優れており、リソース制約や高スループットの計算シナリオに柔軟に対応可能です。

papers.title: Who Grades the Agent? Privilege Separation for Coding-Agent Benchmarks
papers.summary: Benchmarks for AI-based coding agents are a staple of the current AI landscape, because they are the leading way to measure the performance of LLMs. Their scores guide business and research decisions. Evaluating coding agents is challenging, since they are able to manipulate their evaluation infrastructure to artificially achieve better scores. Grading an agent's solution often requires running its code, which can then manipulate the evaluation process. BenchJack, an automated benchmark auditor, recently reached near-perfect scores on nine of ten popular agent benchmarks without actually solving their tasks. Agents already do this unprompted, as OpenAI's July 2026 Hugging Face incident showed. Building on secure systems design, we introduce SplitBench, a privilege separation framework for evaluating coding agents and the first in the scientific literature to separate running a task's tests from judging their results. Even an agent whose code takes over the entire test environment cannot forge a pass, because a trusted grader holds the expected answers. We show that real-world benchmarks (e.g., Terminal-Bench, DeepSWE) can be ported to the SplitBench framework with minimal effort and high fidelity: 180 of 202 tasks convert, and SplitBench agrees with the native graders on 98.7% of agent attempts. We attack the converted tasks in the worst case, where adversarial agents can read all the grading code but not the expected answers. SplitBench blocked 75% of their attempts; the rest mostly reveal weaknesses in the original tasks' tests rather than flaws in SplitBench.
papers.tldr: AIベースのコーディングエージェントの評価において、評価プロセスを操作する問題を解決するために、タスクのテスト実行と結果評価を分離する「SplitBench」というフレームワークが提案され、実際のベンチマークにおいて高い精度で機能することが示されました。

papers.title: ENC-QA: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Electronic Navigational Charts
papers.summary: Nautical charts encode safety-critical maritime information through standardized symbols, attributes, text, and heterogeneous geometries. Interpreting these charts and assessing the navigational significance of successive chart updates requires recognizing nautical features, determining their spatial relationships, and applying navigational knowledge. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising approach to nautical-chart interpretation, yet systematic evaluation of their fine-grained nautical feature recognition, chart-based spatial reasoning, and application of navigational knowledge to assessing chart changes remains limited. We introduce ENC-QA, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 77,312 questions derived from 6,612 National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Electronic Navigational Charts (ENCs). The benchmark evaluates four complementary capabilities: ENC Perception, Spatial Reasoning, Joint Perception and Spatial Reasoning, and Application. Of these, 8,227 questions form a progressive subset that decomposes selected chart-change cases into linked questions progressing from change detection to criticality assessment, enabling case-level analysis of how models use perceptual and spatial evidence to determine the navigational significance of chart changes. Evaluations of 10 open-weight VLMs reveal substantial limitations in fine-grained nautical feature recognition and feature-grounded spatial reasoning. Controlled evidence interventions show that relevant perceptual and spatial information improves change-criticality accuracy. Our findings establish ENC-QA as a diagnostic resource for nautical-chart understanding and safety-critical navigational decisions. We will release the benchmark and evaluation code upon publication.
papers.tldr: ENC-QAは、電子海図における視覚と言語モデルの診断ベンチマークで、77,312の質問を通じて海図の特徴認識や空間推論能力を評価します。評価結果は、モデルの限界を示し、海図の理解と安全な航行判断における重要なリソースとしての役割を果たします。

papers.title: Anchors That Move Without Collapsing: Exclusive-Region Anchor Routing for Vision Transformers
papers.summary: Anchor tokens let a vision transformer exchange global information through a few summaries, but nothing forces different anchors to summarise different things. On one shared backbone we show that a Perceiver-style pathway and an AnchorFormer pathway collapse to a single summary, the latter despite its mass normalisation (pooling-map similarity 0.99), while other soft pathways, including Representative Attention, stay partly redundant (0.59-0.79). These results concern the routing modules inside our block, not the full published models. An exclusive partition of the patch grid cannot collapse by construction, and matched component by component it is 2.4-3.6 points more accurate than Representative Attention on CIFAR-100. We then propose focus anchors, which place most anchors at the peaks of a learned importance map while all anchors keep one exclusive Voronoi partition. Focus anchors beat a fixed partition on a cluttered canvas (+1.5 points, 95% CI [0.5, 2.6]) but not on full-HD traffic-sign recognition. There, both variants match dense attention with local windows at about a fifth of its FLOPs, and the fixed partition also trains 1.5x faster per step than dense attention with FlashAttention, though both use more memory; a ViT on a downsampled input loses half its mean average precision. Hard exclusive assignment is the only region assignment we tested that is both stable and most accurate: softmax and Sinkhorn relaxations diverge, and Gumbel-softmax trains but is less accurate. We also report the limits: a ResNet-18 is more accurate on every task we trained it on in this from-scratch regime, and anchors train faster than FlashAttention only from about 1536x1536 pixels and never use less memory.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: 本研究では、Vision Transformerにおけるアンカートークンの新しいルーティング手法「Exclusive-Region Anchor Routing」を提案し、焦点を当てたアンカーが従来の手法よりも精度を向上させることを示しましたが、ResNet-18には及ばない結果となりました。

papers.title: DGC-Net: A Depth-Geometric Conditioning Network for Projection-Supervised OCTA Segmentation
papers.summary: OCTA segmentation is commonly formulated as a projection supervised task: models observe 3D volumetric scans but are supervised by 2D en-face semantic maps. Existing 2D and 3D-to-2D methods either discard axial information or compress depth responses into latent projections, leaving vessel crossings, diffuse capillary regions, and FAZ boundaries vulnerable to projection-induced ambiguity. We propose DGC-Net, a Depth-Geometric Conditioning Network that recasts 3D-to-2D OCTA segmentation as depth-geometrically conditioned prediction, where projected features are decoded with compact descriptors of axial vascular evidence. DGC-Net preserves local depth geometry through Depth-Moment Conditioning (DM), which injects axial localization and dispersion cues into the projection stream, and captures global depth layout through Holistic Depth-Geometry Modulation (HDM), which derives a raw-volume axial prior for final 2D decoding. Experiments on the OCTA-500 6mm and 3mm subsets show that DGC-Net achieves 83.58% and 88.62% mIoU, respectively, reaching state-of-the-art performance.
papers.tldr: DGC-Netは、深さ幾何学的条件付けネットワークを用いて、3Dから2DへのOCTAセグメンテーションを再構築し、軸方向の血管情報を保持しながら投影による曖昧さを軽減する手法で、OCTA-500データセットで最先端の性能を達成しました。

papers.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
papers.summary: Multi-agent systems for scientific claim verification increasingly rely on role-structured LLM debate to pressure-test hypotheses. However, when debating agents are instantiated from the same underlying base model, they share identical latent representations, making self-critique bias structurally inevitable. Static fixed-iteration protocols compound this by either halting prematurely before evidence stabilizes or wasting inference compute after convergence. We present \sys{}, a multi-agent research verification framework that addresses both failure modes. First, we introduce an asymmetric role architecture comprising an Advocate, Skeptic, and Arbitrator with opposing epistemic directives, producing significantly lower role-embedding similarity (0.852 vs.\ 0.918 for symmetric Multi-Agent Debate [MAD], $p = 5.82 \times 10^{-8}$) and surfacing more contested claims (22.0\% vs.\ 15.4\%). Second, we propose the Belief-Delta ($\DB$) convergence criterion, an evidence-grounded stopping rule that eliminates over-iteration (0.0\% vs.\ 62.5\% for Fixed-$3$) while cutting LLM calls by 2.4$\times$. Third, each supported claim is anchored to a verbatim literature snippet audited by an independent NLI classifier, achieving a 21.7\% hallucination rate (comparable to 25.9\% for a Self-Refine critic, $p = 0.61$) while establishing auditable evidence grounding. Across 200 runs on 40 research hypotheses evaluated with DeepSeek-R1-32B, \sys{} balances compute efficiency with rigorous epistemic verification.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: \sys{}は、役割構造を持つマルチエージェントシステムを用いて科学的主張の検証を行い、自己批判バイアスを軽減するために非対称な役割アーキテクチャと証拠に基づく収束基準を導入し、計算効率と厳密な検証を両立させるフレームワークです。

papers.title: Auditable Financial Knowledge Graphs: Schema-Driven Construction and Intrinsic Quality Evaluation
papers.summary: Financial documents combine narrative disclosures, accounting metrics, corporate structures, management commentary, and time-dependent facts, making them difficult to represent using conventional chunk-based retrieval-augmented generation systems. This paper presents an auditable, schema-driven methodology for constructing temporal financial knowledge graphs from page-delimited documents parsed using a general purpose document intelligence service. Overlapping document windows undergo phased large language model extraction of structural entities, quantitative observations, and domain-specific relationships. Candidate graph elements are validated against predefined schemas and consolidated through scope-aware exact, normalized, fuzzy, embedding-based, and LLM-assisted entity resolution. Temporal merge constraints, deterministic edge deduplication, conflict-aware property management, and fine-grained provenance preserve issuer identity, reporting-period validity, and traceability to source evidence. The contributions of this work comprise the proposed methodology for financial knowledge graph construction, the creation of an evidence-grounded temporal knowledge graph from heterogeneous financial documents, and an intrinsic framework for evaluating the quality of the resulting graph. The evaluation framework assesses seven weighted dimensions, two hard validation gates, and structural diagnostics. By separating graph-quality assessment from downstream retrieval and answer generation, the framework supports systematic diagnosis and iterative refinement of the constructed graph.
papers.tldr: この論文では、財務文書から時間依存の財務知識グラフを構築するための監査可能なスキーマ駆動型手法を提案し、構造的エンティティや定量的観察を抽出し、事前定義されたスキーマに基づいて候補グラフ要素を検証・統合する方法を示しています。また、グラフの品質評価のための内在的フレームワークを提供し、構築されたグラフの系統的診断と反復的改良を支援します。

papers.title: DistDNA: Language Model Fingerprinting under Stochastic Decoding
papers.summary: Behavioral fingerprints identify a large language model (LLM) from its responses to a shared set of prompts, enabling applications such as verifying whether a deployed model corresponds to the checkpoint it claims to be. Deployed models, however, are commonly served with stochastic decoding, under which the same model may produce different responses to an identical prompt, depending on an unknown temperature and top-$p$ setting. Existing representations such as LLM DNA provide limited treatment of this variation. A natural remedy is to characterize models by their response distributions, which, however, raises two challenges. First, each distribution must be estimated from only a small number of sampled responses. Second, a change in decoding setting can alter responses to the same extent as a change of checkpoint. Consequently, fingerprint distances alone provide an incomplete basis for model identity, and identification typically relies on a classifier trained jointly on fingerprints from many checkpoints. We propose DistDNA, which represents a model by its prompt-conditional response distributions and compares models by promptwise maximum mean discrepancy (MMD). The model under examination is assigned to the known checkpoint whose reference fingerprints, collected at several decoding settings, lie nearest to its own, without training a classifier. We show that finite sampling adds variance-dependent terms to the expected squared fingerprint distance, with these terms decreasing as $O(1/R)$ for equal response counts, where $R$ is the number of responses per prompt. Experiments across 115 model checkpoint entries demonstrate that DistDNA improves identification accuracy over the strongest baseline, LLM DNA, by 10.36%.
papers.tldr: DistDNAは、確率的デコーディング下での大規模言語モデル（LLM）の行動指紋を特定する手法で、モデルの応答分布を用いて識別精度を向上させることを提案しており、実験では従来のLLM DNAよりも10.36%の精度向上を示した。

papers.title: Graph Signal Generation via Graph-Aware Diffusion Models
papers.summary: Many signals are defined on the nodes of a graph, such as traffic flow at road sensors or user purchases of related products. They are often partly observed, and learning their distribution enables imputing missing values and forecasting future ones. Diffusion models learn such distributions, but their forward noise is independent across nodes and does not depend on the graph. We introduce graph-aware diffusion (GAD), whose forward process is a heat diffusion on the graph driven by Gaussian noise. In the graph Fourier basis, the forward transition is a scalar Gaussian channel at each frequency. With a shared diffusion rate, high graph frequencies are attenuated faster than low ones. We propose Mode-Adaptive SNR Scheduling (MASS), which assigns each graph frequency its own diffusion rate and keeps all of them at the same SNR. For graph-stationary signals, MASS equalizes the normalized error of the optimal linear denoiser across frequencies. We bound reverse-SDE stiffness as a function of the (shifted) Laplacian's condition number, with a logarithmic upper bound for MASS and a linear lower bound for shared rates. GAD with MASS improves recommendation accuracy by 5-19%, reduces traffic-imputation RMSE by up to 7.8% with half as many reverse steps, and improves forecasting MAE and RMSE using only 3 reverse steps.
papers.tldr: グラフ信号生成のためのグラフ対応拡散モデル（GAD）を提案し、モード適応SNRスケジューリング（MASS）を用いて、グラフ上の信号の分布を学習することで、推薦精度を5-19%向上させ、交通データの欠損値補完のRMSEを最大7.8%削減しました。

papers.title: Mixture of Latent Recursions for Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.summary: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) performs task-specific adaptation using a fixed low-rank architecture, whose expressiveness is typically increased by enlarging or adding learnable modules with a proportional parameter overhead. We introduce Mixture of Latent Recursions (MoLR), an adaptive recursion framework that enhances adaptation expressiveness while preserving parameter efficiency. MoLR recursively refines the down-projected latent representation of each input using a shared transformation. A lightweight threshold-based router independently determines whether each token should undergo further refinement, while dynamically adjusted thresholds encourage balanced utilization across recursion depths. Extensive experiments across diverse language and vision tasks demonstrate that MoLR consistently outperforms representative LoRA variants with negligible parameter overhead over LoRA. Further analyses show that MoLR learns input-dependent recursion-depth allocation and enables a controllable inference-time compute-performance trade-off without requiring retraining. Code will be publicly available.
papers.tldr: Mixture of Latent Recursions (MoLR)は、Low-Rank Adaptation（LoRA）の効率を保ちながら適応表現力を向上させるフレームワークで、入力ごとにダウンプロジェクトされた潜在表現を再帰的に洗練し、トークンごとに独立した軽量なルーターがさらなる洗練を決定します。実験結果では、MoLRがLoRAの代表的なバリエーションをわずかなパラメータオーバーヘッドで上回ることが示されています。

papers.title: Underwater Spectral Recovery via Multi-View Hyperspectral Imaging
papers.summary: Underwater imaging suffers from wavelength-dependent absorption and scattering that distort scenes and obscure spectral signatures. While RGB restoration improves visual clarity, the outputs remain broadband and tied to the sensor's color space. We introduce a physically grounded framework that lifts underwater restoration to continuous spectral radiance using multi-view hyperspectral imaging. By representing continuous spectra via low-rank basis functions and leveraging multi-distance observations, our framework jointly constrains scene radiance and water parameters. We employ a robust sparse-to-dense pipeline: water parameters are estimated from consistent multi-view matches and then applied globally to invert the light transport model across the full images. Validated on physics-based synthetic data rendered via the Mitsuba 3 spectral path tracer, our method recovers physically meaningful radiance spectra and, as a downstream application, outperforms standard image restoration baselines.
papers.tldr: 水中画像は波長依存の吸収と散乱により歪みが生じますが、提案されたフレームワークはマルチビューのハイパースペクトルイメージングを用いて連続スペクトル放射を復元し、物理的に意味のある放射スペクトルを回復します。この手法は、従来の画像復元手法を上回る性能を示しています。

papers.title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models
papers.summary: We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: 本研究では、格子ゲージ理論のサンプリングにおいて、ゲージ等価な拡散モデルを用い、2次元U(2)場構成の正確なサンプリングを実現し、4次元SU(3)に対しても初期の有望な結果を示しました。

papers.title: Autonomous quantum machine learning via Riemannian gradient-based optimization
papers.summary: Quantum machine learning models typically rely on repeated quantum measurements and classical optimization during training, making the quantum-to-classical information-extraction process a fundamental bottleneck for scalability. We propose a framework for autonomous self-training quantum machine learning, based on Riemannian gradient optimization, in which the optimization proceeds entirely within the quantum domain without requiring quantum measurements or classical feedback. We derive the Riemannian gradient update rules for a broad class of learning tasks and identify sufficient conditions under which the resulting training dynamics can be realized fully autonomously. Within this regime, we establish an exponential convergence guarantee, in the training iterations, for sufficiently small step sizes, and further analyze the training cost in terms of the growth of the circuit depth. Importantly, we further show that the trained model can automatically discover symmetries hidden in the training data without $\textit{a priori}$ specification. For the canonical examples of quantum phase classification and unitary learning with a hidden symmetry, our numerical study indicates that learning can be achieved at low circuit depths with only a few distinct training examples. Our results thus establish autonomous quantum machine learning as a promising paradigm that removes the classical optimization loop while retaining strong theoretical guarantees and practical performances.
papers.tldr: 量子機械学習の新しいフレームワークを提案し、リーマン勾配最適化を用いて量子ドメイン内で完全に自律的に学習を行うことが可能であることを示しました。このアプローチにより、量子測定や古典的フィードバックなしでのトレーニングが実現され、隠れた対称性を自動的に発見できることが確認されました。

papers.title: Redesigning Neural Networks to Not be Confidently Wrong even to Strong Adversarial Attacks
papers.summary: Early deep learning models attempted to simulate visual perception using a neural hierarchy that alternated between two types of layer: one modelled on cortical simple cells (that was designed to increase selectivity), and one modelled on cortical complex cells (that aimed to increase tolerance). We show that such a neural network (NN) architecture, when implemented with novel components that are better able to learn selective and tolerant representations, is capable of accurate and robust image classification and improved alignment between the behaviour of the model and the perceptual abilities of humans. Firstly, the proposed models are shallow, fewer than ten layer-pairs, which is more consistent with the rapid feedforward object categorisation performed by the biological visual system. Secondly, they are far less prone to producing classification predictions with high confidence for samples from unknown classes or for image consisting of pure noise, and hence, like humans are not easily fooled into perceiving objects that are not present in the image. Thirdly, for the proposed NNs adversarial samples cause predictions with low confidence, enabling them to be accurately identified. In contrast to humans, our networks still do not correctly classify adversarial samples. However, the behaviour of our networks is a significant step towards human-like behaviour compared to standard DNNs that produce highly confident, but incorrect, classification predictions for adversarial samples. The increased robustness to adversarial and unknown samples is achieved while maintaining competitive performance in terms of generalisation to novel samples from the training categories. This enables models of this type to be competitive with state-of-the-art DNNs across multiple different evaluation metrics and benchmark tasks.
papers.tldr: 新しい神経ネットワークアーキテクチャは、選択的かつ耐性のある表現を学習することで、画像分類の精度と堅牢性を向上させ、未知のクラスやノイズに対して高い自信を持った誤った予測を減少させることができる。これにより、従来の深層ニューラルネットワークと比較して、人間に近い行動を示しつつ、競争力のあるパフォーマンスを維持することが可能となる。

papers.title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech
papers.summary: Audio language models (ALMs) can answer clinical questions from speech, outperforming baselines built on handcrafted acoustic features. Reasoning ALMs generate a chain of thought that refers to properties of the speaker's voice before predicting. Each statement the model makes about the voice needs to be checked against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording. On clinical speech, existing evaluations score only the final answer. We introduce Speech Language Pathologist Bench (SLP-Bench), a benchmark grading each acoustic claim in the chain of thought against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording.
